methods.interviews: Seven semistructured interviews, November–December 2016, Marrakech COP22 and Bonn. Six official delegation members who attended at least one target conference: two EU negotiators, one African-country negotiator, one AOSIS representative, one LDC representative and one Western climate scientist accredited by Uganda; plus a climate-policy expert.
methods.missing_perspectives: No Chinese, Indian or Brazilian negotiators interviewed; author explicitly acknowledges this.
methods.interview_analysis: Opening comparative question, then theory-guided questions; cooperation model shown to respondents at end. Transcribed and coded in MaxQDA. Transcripts and independent reliability assessment not supplied in article.
methods.speech_act_data: Earth Negotiations Bulletin summaries, not official verbatim transcripts. Cooperative or conflictual statements toward other actors coded.
methods.unequal_windows: Copenhagen conference compared with Paris plus June, August and October 2015 Bonn meetings to compensate for informal Paris negotiations not covered by the dataset.
methods.thresholds: Approximately 1,200–1,300 relative speech acts in each comparison window. Major actors require at least 60 appearances as speaker/addressee. Reciprocal relation requires at least one-third returned acts and at least four total acts. Author acknowledges arbitrary threshold and assumed speaking order.
methods.limits: Reported positional alignment does not measure accepted concessions. United States excluded from Copenhagen major-actor network; no separate China national node in Paris figure. No matched China–US causal estimate; no direct observation of Chinese instructions.

decisive_locators.use: Attributed mechanism concerning trust in presidency; not a Chinese concession decision.

decisive_locators.source_dependence: Substantially draws on Falkner 2016 and other scholarship; treaty originals control exact legal obligations. Do not import claim that fairness disputes disappeared.

decisive_locators.claim: EU negotiator interviewed December 2, 2016 describes Chinese concern about blame and European leaders linking climate to bilateral business.
decisive_locators.use: Foreign participant assessment of reputation pressure, not independently established Chinese motive or a documented exchange of specified concessions.

decisive_locators.claim: Paris/Bonn relations graph and broader coalitions.
decisive_locators.source_dependence: Brazil High Ambition Coalition account cites Brun 2016; it is not another original Högl interview.

decisive_locators.claim: Author bounds reciprocity: red-line crossing unlikely; reciprocal cooperation can reinforce relationships and positions.
decisive_locators.use: Useful limit on relationship-based explanation; not an estimated effect.

precision_notes: The article describes the 2014 announcement on p.373 too broadly as China first announcing emission reductions. Existing dated primary source specifies a prospective CO2 peak and non-fossil share; no immediate economy-wide absolute reduction or full-GHG cap is inferred.
The article contrasts its approximately 40–50 percent reciprocity with laboratory rates. Different units and designs do not support a matched numerical comparison of negotiation effectiveness.
Reputation was not demonstrably absent from Copenhagen. Existing participant evidence prevents treating its later prominence as a newly introduced national motive.

methods.locator: Printed p.2 and complete notes pp.22–27
methods.design: Approximately 25 interviews in early 2014 plus existing scholarship, official policies, statistics, journalism and policy publications. Notes identify roles/dates; no full selection protocol, transcripts or systematic coding account.
methods.sample_boundary: Includes researchers advising government, a researcher also on Chinese climate delegation, provincial official, NGO staff, consultants, an energy state-enterprise member and Beijing-based UN official. Not 25 Chinese negotiators or officials.
methods.temporal_value: Interviews/publication precede November 2014 joint announcement and Paris; reported uncertainty is prospective rather than hindsight.
methods.thematic_boundary: Primarily mitigation; forestry treated as beyond scope in note 9. Does not reconstruct decision on a particular US–China text.
methods.visual_limits: Historical statistics and projections remain dated data. Projected energy use is not realized later emissions. No units inferred where chart axes omit them.

unselected_leads: Hilton–Kerr 2017 and Yu–Zhu 2015 identified during screening but not fully acquired/read and not counted. Högl 2018 English working paper located but not read or counted as a separate study. No new reading claim for pre-existing climate sources.
chapter_implications: Supplement Xie target-selection passage with prospective domestic-feasibility evidence; distinguish intensity, fuel share, local pollution and an absolute CO2 peak.
Add one attributed presidency-trust mechanism beyond Stern–Xie rapport, without inferring Chinese motives from AOSIS/LDC interviews.
Keep national ambition distinct from international procedure and implementation. Existing primary treaty sources control the legal account.
Preserve contemporaneous disagreement and existing Copenhagen flexibility; do not portray a national shift from rigidity to cooperation.
No claim that Xi centralization or a specific internal routing change caused concession flexibility.
